name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
summary: A wide-stance squat holding one dumbbell between the legs. It keeps the torso upright, trains the quads and glutes, and is gentle to learn at home.
setup: Stand with feet clearly wider than shoulder width and toes turned out about 30-45 degrees.
Hold one end of a dumbbell with both hands in front of your hips, arms straight. A heavy backpack held by its top handle also works.
Lift your chest and brace your trunk.
execution: Bend your knees and push them out over your toes as you lower straight down between your feet.
Keep your torso tall while the dumbbell hangs between your legs.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, or as deep as you can control.
Push through your whole foot and squeeze your glutes to stand up.
mistakes: Knees caving inward: push them out in line with the toes and widen the stance a little.
Leaning forward: keep the chest up and the weight close to the body.
Heels lifting: shift weight to the midfoot and heel, and reduce depth if needed.
Toes turned out too far for your hips: use an angle that lets your knees track comfortably over your feet.

references.title: Dumbbell Sumo Squat: Cues & Common Mistakes
references.author: Katie Orlic
